I’m not able to pull SSL‑certificate history directly from here, but I can point you toward a few ways you can do it yourself:

| Method | What you’ll need | How to use it |
|--------|------------------|---------------|
| **crt.sh** | Free public search | Go to <https://crt.sh/> and type `reddit.com` in the search box. You’ll see a list of all certificates issued for that domain (and sub‑domains) along with issuance dates, issuers, and the certificate’s SHA‑256 fingerprint. |
| **Qualys SSL Labs** | Free public scan | Visit <https://www.ssllabs.com/ssltest/> and enter `reddit.com`. The “Certificate” tab will show the chain and the validity period. |
| **Censys** | Requires an account (free tier available) | Use the Censys API or web UI to query `dns.names:reddit.com AND services.tls.certificates`. |
| **Shodan** | Requires an account | Search for `org:"reddit.com"` or use the TLS certificate search. |
| **Google Certificate Transparency logs** | Free | Use the Google CT log viewer at <https://transparencyreport.google.com/https/ct> and search for `reddit.com`. |

If you have a specific API key (e.g., for Censys, Shodan, or another service), let me know which service it belongs to and I can give you a quick example of how to call that API. Otherwise, the above free tools should give you a comprehensive view of the certificate history for `reddit.com`.
